findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: An attacker could supply a specially crafted input that causes atoi to return an unexpected value, leading to incorrect memory allocation or access.
findings.assumptions: The input is expected to be a valid integer, but the code does not handle invalid input gracefully.

findings.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
findings.trigger: An attacker could supply a very large value for N, causing integer overflow and leading to incorrect memory allocation or access.
findings.assumptions: The input is expected to be a valid integer, but the code does not check for overflow conditions.

findings.title: Improper Release of Resources
findings.trigger: An attacker could supply a very large value for N, causing the creation of a large number of child processes, leading to resource exhaustion.
findings.assumptions: The input is expected to be a valid integer, but the code does not limit the number of child processes created.

findings.title: Lack of Error Handling
findings.trigger: An attacker could supply invalid input that causes atoi to return an unexpected value, leading to incorrect memory allocation or access.
findings.assumptions: The input is expected to be a valid integer, but the code does not handle invalid input gracefully.
